Initially created: 2026-03-28T20:03:58.807+09:00 by CH Translate the following text from Classical Chinese into English.
Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the English translation.
5. The target language is English.

p.seg: 《Ancient Text》.
He feasted with the Son of Heaven on top of Juān Mountain.
On the day Wùyín,
the Son of Heaven campaigned northward,
and then crossed the Zhāng River.
On the day Gēngchén,
he arrived at □,
and feasted the Son of Heaven upon a flat rock.
The Son of Heaven then performed grand music.
He stood in his carriage without resting,
until reaching the foot of Xíng Mountain.
On the day Guǐwèi,
snow fell,
and the Son of Heaven hunted on the western slope of Xíng Mountain.
Thereupon, he managed to cross the pass of Xíng Mountain,
and proceeded north along the northern bank of the Hūtuó River.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Son of Heaven ascended northward to □.
The Son of Heaven campaigned northward against the Quǎnróng.
The Quǎnróng □ Hú feasted the Son of Heaven on the northern bank of the Dāng River.
The Son of Heaven was pleased,
and □ rewarded the warriors of the Seven Elite Troops with battle.
On the day Gēngyín,
north winds brought rain and snow.
Because of the cold,
the Son of Heaven ordered his royal retinue to rest.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Son of Heaven campaigned westward,
and then crossed the Yú Pass.
On the day Jǐhài,
he arrived at the plains of Yānjū Yúzhī.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Son of Heaven campaigned westward,
arriving at the Péng people.
The descendant of the Hé Zōng, Péng Bóxù, came to meet the Son of Heaven at Zhì’s □.
He presented first ten leopard skins and twelve fine horses.
The Son of Heaven sent Jǐng Lì to receive them.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Son of Heaven lodged at Qīzhuó,
and then fished westward in the river.
To observe □ Zhì’s □.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Son of Heaven hunted at Shèn Marsh.
There he obtained a white fox and a black raccoon dog,
and used them to sacrifice to the Hé Zōng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ.
The Son of Heaven drank on the banks of the river.
The Son of Heaven assembled the men of the six armies south of Péng State, above Shèn Marsh.
On the day Wùyín,
the Son of Heaven campaigned westward,
traveling swiftly,
until reaching Yángyū Mountain,
where Hé Bó Wúyí had his capital,
this being the Hé Zōng clan.
Hé Zōng Bó Yāo came to meet the Son of Heaven at Yānrán Mountain.
He presented as gifts bundles of silk with added jade discs,
first a white □,
the Son of Heaven sent Guǎng Fù to receive them.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Son of Heaven held a grand assembly at Yān □ Mountain, on the banks of the river.
He then ordered Jǐng Lì and Liáng Gù,
to lead the six armies.
The Son of Heaven appointed an auspicious day, Wùwǔ.
The Son of Heaven wore grand attire:
ceremonial cap and robes,
sash and belt,
holding a tablet,
with pendants on both sides,
holding a jade disc,
standing facing south below the cold.
The Chief Invocator assisted him.
The officials presented a complete set of five sacrificial animals □.
The Son of Heaven presented the jade disc to the Hé Zōng.
Hé Zōng Bó Yāo received the disc,
faced west and sank the disc into the river,
bowing twice and touching his head to the ground.
The Invocator sank oxen, horses, pigs, and sheep.
Hé Zōng □ commanded the August Son of Heaven,
Hé Bó proclaimed:
"The Emperor says:
'Mù Mǎn,
you shall forever devote yourself to the affairs of the times!'"
Facing south, he bowed twice.
Hé Zōng again proclaimed:
"The Emperor says:
'Mù Mǎn,
I show you the treasures of Chōng Mountain,
instruct you that at Kūnlún □ there are four level springs and seventy,
and you shall reach the hills of Kūnlún,
to view the treasures of Chōng Mountain.
I grant you the words of obscurity.'"
The Son of Heaven received the command,
facing south, bowed twice.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Son of Heaven held a grand assembly at Huáng Mountain.
He then unrolled maps and examined the canon,
to view the treasures of the Son of Heaven.
It said:
"The treasures of the Son of Heaven:
jade fruits, xuán pearls, candle silver, and golden ointment.
The treasures of the Son of Heaven are worth ten thousand gold □ treasures one hundred gold,
the treasures of a scholar are worth fifty gold,
the treasures of a common man are worth ten gold.
The Son of Heaven’s bow shoots men,
his sword steps,
oxen and horses,
rhinoceros □ vessels are worth a thousand gold.
The Son of Heaven’s horses run a thousand lǐ,
surpassing men and fierce beasts.
The Son of Heaven’s dogs run a hundred lǐ,
and seize tigers and leopards."
Bó Yāo said:
"Birds of prey use their wings:
said □ crows and kites, kūnjī fly eight hundred lǐ.
Famous beasts use their feet:
□ run a thousand lǐ,
suānní □ wild horses run five hundred lǐ,
qióngqióng jùxū run a hundred lǐ,
elk □ twenty lǐ."
It said:
"Bó Yāo, having presented the river canon,
then rode in a carriage drawn by Qú Huáng horses to lead the way for the Son of Heaven,
to reach the western lands."
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Son of Heaven crossed the river westward.
□ Here were warm valleys and joyful capitals,
where the Hé Zōng clan roamed and dwelled.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Son of Heaven ordered his officials to present vessels.
He then ordered Zhèng Gōng Jiāo Fù,
to receive the edict and regulations,
to deploy the team of eight steeds.
To drink within the branches of the Zhǐ River,
south of the Jīshí River.
The Son of Heaven’s steeds:
Chì Jì, Dào Lí, Bái Yì, Yú Lún, Shān Zǐ, Qú Huáng, Huá Liú, Lǜ Ěr;
dogs:
Zhòng Gōng, Chè Zhǐ, Guàn Jiā, □ Huáng, Nán □, Lái Bái.
The Son of Heaven’s charioteers:
Zào Fǔ, Sān Bǎi, Gěng Xiāo, Sháo Jí.
It said:
"The Son of Heaven with these goes out □ into marshes,
hunting and fishing with bow and line."
The Son of Heaven said:
"Alas!
I, the One Man, am not full of virtue,
but am skilled in pleasures,
will later generations also recount my faults!"
The warriors of the Seven Elite Troops □ the Son of Heaven said:
"What later generations hope for,
is not to lose the constant ways of Heaven.
When farmers and artisans have their gains,
men and women have clothing and food.
The common people treasure wealth,
officials perform their duties.
Thus Heaven has its seasons,
the people □ clans respond.
□ What need to scheme for pleasure?
What intention is forgotten?
Sharing benefits with the people,
this generation takes as constant."
The Son of Heaven praised them,
and bestowed upon them a left-worn pendant of jade splendor.
Then they bowed twice and touched their heads to the ground.
《Ancient Text》.
□ Bó Yāo said:
□ He enfeoffed Mó Zhòu on the northern bank of the river,
to be the master of the Yīn people.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Son of Heaven ascended southwest to □ where the master dwelled.
Here were great trees and abundant grasses,
here were wild beasts,
suitable for hunting.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the people of □ Jū Lǜ presented a hundred □ of wine to the Son of Heaven.
The Son of Heaven drank and then departed,
and subsequently lodged at the slopes of Kūnlún,
on the northern bank of the Chì River.
On the auspicious day of Xīnyǒu,
the Son of Heaven ascended the Kūnlún Mountains,
to view the palace of Huángdì,
and to enclose the tomb of Fēnglóng,
to proclaim it to later generations.
On Guǐhài,
the Son of Heaven prepared pure and complete sacrificial animals,
to perform the yīn sacrifice at the Kūnlún Mountains.
On Jiǎzǐ,
the Son of Heaven campaigned northward,
and lodged at the Pearl Marsh.
He fished in the flowing waters.
He said:
"The marsh of the Pearl Marsh
measures thirty lǐ square."
Here there were rushes, reeds, sedges, and cattails,
thatch, fù grass, reeds, and yāo grass.
The people of the Pearl Marsh then offered white jade... pieces,
... horns of one,
... three,
which could be used for... washing.
Then they presented food,
... wine ten...,
gū and qiāng nine...
Their flavors were like deer tripe and were smooth.
Thereupon they offered three hundred horses for food,
three thousand cattle and sheep.
The Son of Heaven... Kūnlún,
to guard the palace of Huángdì,
overseeing the Chìshuǐ to the south,
and guarding the treasures of the Chōngshān to the north.
The Son of Heaven then bestowed upon... people... wú, three to five gold rings.
Thirty vermilion belts adorned with cowries.
Four gōngbù cloths.
... wú then prostrated in worship and received them.
The Son of Heaven also gave them two times six yellow oxen,
to... thirty people at the Kūnlún Mountains.
In the late summer, on Dīngmǎo,
the Son of Heaven ascended northward to the top of the Chōngshān,
to gaze upon the four wilds,
and said:
"Chōngshān,
this is indeed the highest mountain under heaven."
The zìmùhuá flower fears not the snow,
the Son of Heaven then took the fruit of the zìmùhuá flower,
and carried it back to plant it.
He said:
"The marsh of Chōngshān,
where clear water springs forth,
warm and gentle without wind,
is where the flying birds and hundred beasts drink and feed,
what the former kings called Xuánpǔ."
The Son of Heaven then obtained jade blossoms and branches of sī.
He said:
"Chōngshān,
is where the hundred beasts gather,
and where the flying birds roost."
Here there were... beasts,
that ate tigers and leopards like deer and bore bones,
pán... beginning like elk,
with small heads and large noses.
Here there were red leopards, white tigers, bears, brown bears, jackals, wolves, wild horses, wild oxen, mountain goats, and wild boars.
Here there were white sǔn and green diāo,
that seized dogs and sheep,
and ate boars and deer.
It is said the Son of Heaven observed for five days upon Chōngshān,
then inscribed a record upon Xuánpǔ,
to proclaim it to later generations.
On Rénshēn,
the Son of Heaven campaigned westward.
On Jiǎxū,
he reached Chìwū.
The people of Chìwū... offered a thousand hú of wine to the Son of Heaven,
nine hundred horses for food,
three thousand sheep and cattle,
and a hundred loads of jì and wheat.
The Son of Heaven sent Jìfù to receive them.
He said:
"The Chìwū clan originally came from the Zhōu lineage.
When Tàiwáng Dǎnfǔ first established the western lands,
he enfeoffed his eldest son Wú Tàibó in Eastern Wú,
instructing him with the punishment of metal blades,
and bestowed the jade of the Zhōu house.
He enfeoffed his favored minister Cháng Jìchuò at the foot of Chōngshān,
giving him his eldest daughter in marriage,
instructing him with the punishment of jade and stone,
to act as master of the Zhōu house."
The Son of Heaven then bestowed upon the people of Chìwū... four black chariots,
forty yì of gold,
fifty sets of cowrie belts,
and three hundred bundles of pearls.
... then prostrated in worship and received them.
He said:
"... mountain,
is indeed the finest mountain under heaven.
Where precious jade is found.
Fine grains grow there,
and plants and trees are lush and beautiful."
The Son of Heaven then took the fine grain and returned,
planting it in the Central States.
It is said the Son of Heaven rested for five days below... mountain,
then performed the guǎngyuè music.
The people of Chìwū... offered beautiful women to the Son of Heaven.
Women skilled in music and women of rank became his favorites.
He said:
"The land of the Chìwū clan,
is a land of beautiful people,
and where precious jade is found."
On Jǐmǎo,
the Son of Heaven campaigned northward,
Zhao traveled... lodged.
On Gēngchén,
he crossed the Yángshuǐ.
On Xīnsì,
he entered Cáonú.
The people of Cáonú, Xì, toasted the Son of Heaven on the Yángshuǐ,
and offered nine hundred horses for food,
seven thousand cattle and sheep,
and a hundred carts of jì grain.
The Son of Heaven sent Péng Gù to receive them.
The Son of Heaven then bestowed upon the people of Cáonú, Xì... a gold deer,
a silver elk,
forty cowrie belts,
and four hundred bundles of pearls.
Xì then prostrated in worship and received them.
On Rénwǔ,
the Son of Heaven campaigned northward,
turning eastward.
On Jiǎshēn,
he reached the Hēishuǐ,
what the Xīmó call Hónglù.
Then it rained for seven days.
The Son of Heaven left the six armies and their followers.
The Son of Heaven then enfeoffed Chánggōng west of the Hēishuǐ river.
This is above Hónglù,
to act as master of the Zhōu house.
This is called the state of Liúxū.
On Xīnmǎo,
the Son of Heaven campaigned northward,
turning eastward,
and followed the Hēishuǐ.
On Guǐsì,
he reached the Qúnyù Mountains.
What Róngchéng shì guarded.
He said:
"The Qúnyù field mountains,
... know,
level and without peril,
four directions straight as a plumb line,
what the former kings called the library.
Sparse in plants and trees and without birds or beasts."
Here there were... trees,
what the Xīmó call...
The Son of Heaven then quarried their jade stones,
taking three chariot-loads of jade tablets,
jade vessels and garments,
and ten thousand pieces of jade.
The Son of Heaven rested for four days at the Qúnyù Mountains,
then ordered the Marquis of Xíng to await the jade workers.
In early autumn, on Dīngyǒu,
the Son of Heaven campaigned northward.
... people, Qiánshí, toasted the Son of Heaven atop Yǔlíng,
and offered fine horses, cattle, and sheep.
Because their state quarried jade stones,
the Son of Heaven did not accept their livestock.
Bó Yāo said:
"... clan,
are descendants of Jiàn..."
The Son of Heaven then bestowed upon them three times six gold urns.
Three hundred bundles of vermilion.
Qiánshí then prostrated in worship and received them.
On the Wùxū day,
the Son of Heaven campaigned westward.
On the Xīnchǒu day,
he arrived at the Jīlǘ clan.
The Son of Heaven then ordered the Jīlǘ clan to supply provisions for the men of the six armies at the foot of Tiě Mountain.
On the Rényín day,
the Son of Heaven sacrificed at Tiě Mountain,
offered sacrifices at the Suburban Gate,
and then removed the sacrificial vessels for the people of the Jīlǘ clan.
Wēnguī then prostrated in reverence and received them.
After the Son of Heaven had sacrificed, he set out,
and then proceeded westward on campaign.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
he arrived at the Fēnghán clan.
Here there were pleasant fields, warm and mild,
where broomcorn millet and wheat grew abundantly,
where dogs, horses, cattle, and sheep flourished,
and where precious jade was [plentiful].
On the Dīngwèi day,
the Son of Heaven held a great assembly on the level plain,
and ordered the troops of the six armies to rest.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
the Son of Heaven held a great feast for the dukes, feudal lords, kings, and the diligent warriors of the Seven Elite Troops on the level plain.
The people of the Fēnghán clan, Wúfú, then presented one hundred fine horses,
three hundred yoked oxen,
seven thousand fine dogs,
two hundred fāng oxen,
three hundred wild horses,
two thousand cattle and sheep,
and three hundred carts of broomcorn millet and wheat.
The Son of Heaven then bestowed upon them four times seven golden and silver urns,
fifty shell-decorated belts,
three hundred bundles of pearls,
and finely carved [objects].
Wúfú, both high and low, prostrated in reverence and received them.
On the Gēngxū day,
the Son of Heaven campaigned westward,
arriving at Xuánchí.
The Son of Heaven rested by Xuánchí,
and had grand music performed,
which lasted for three days before concluding.
This was called the Music Pool.
The Son of Heaven then planted bamboo there,
and this was called the Bamboo Grove.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
the Son of Heaven then proceeded westward on campaign.
On the Bǐngchén day,
he arrived at Kǔ Mountain,
which the Xīmó people called Màoyuàn.
The Son of Heaven then rested and hunted here,
and here he ate bitter [plants].
On the Dīngsì day,
the Son of Heaven campaigned westward.
On the Jǐwèi day,
he lodged at Huángshǔ Mountain,
and then proceeded westward on campaign.
On the Guǐhài day,
he arrived at the state of the Queen Mother of the West.
《Ancient Text》.
On the auspicious day Jiǎzǐ,
the Son of Heaven paid a visit to the Queen Mother of the West.
He held a white jade tablet and a black jade disc to meet the Queen Mother of the West.
He presented fine brocade and silk, one hundred bolts,
and [fine] silk, three hundred bolts.
The Queen Mother of the West bowed twice and received them.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
the Son of Heaven feasted with the Queen Mother of the West by Yáochí.
The Queen Mother of the West sang a ballad for the Son of Heaven,
saying:
"White clouds are in the sky,
and mountains rise from the earth.
The road is long and far,
with rivers and mountains in between.
If you do not die,
might you come again?"
The Son of Heaven replied to her,
saying:
"I shall return to the eastern lands,
and bring harmony to all the Xià.
When the myriad people are equal and at peace,
I will come to see you again.
In about three years,
I shall return to your wilderness."
The Son of Heaven then drove and ascended Yǎn Mountain,
and recorded his traces on the stones of Yǎn Mountain,
planting a pagoda tree there,
and inscribing on it: "Mountain of the Queen Mother of the West."
The people of the world, upon returning from the Mountain of the Queen Mother of the West, composed a lament, singing:
"Having journeyed to the western lands,
we dwelled in her wilderness.
Tigers and leopards were our companions,
and magpies shared our abode.
Her noble decree remains unchanged,
for she is the daughter of the Emperor.
The great mandate of the Son of Heaven is beyond praise, yet we recall the kindness of the people of the world, shedding tears and sobbing.
Playing reed pipes and blowing reeds,
our hearts flutter with emotion.
O sons of the people of the world,
only Heaven's gaze is upon you."
On the Dīngwèi day,
the Son of Heaven drank at Wēn Mountain,
and [observed] birds.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
the Son of Heaven drank by the Rù River,
and issued a decree,
ordering the men of the six armies to [collect] their feathers.
Here there were marshes and wetlands,
here there were hills, plains, and level land.
Large birds shed their feathers.
The men of the six armies all gathered at Kuàngyuán.
It is said the Son of Heaven stayed at Kuàngyuán for three months.
The Son of Heaven held a great feast for the dukes, feudal lords, kings, and the diligent warriors of the Seven Elite Troops atop Yǔlíng,
and had grand music performed.
The men of the six armies hunted freely at Kuàngyuán,
gaining limitless captures.
Birds and beasts were completely driven away.
The men of the six armies hunted grandly for nine days,
then encamped at the [edge] of Yǔlíng,
collecting hides and presenting goods,
loading them onto carts for transport.
The Son of Heaven then loaded one hundred carts with feathers.
On the Jǐhài day,
the Son of Heaven returned eastward,
and the six armies [set out].
On the Gēngzǐ day,
he arrived at [a certain] mountain and rested,
awaiting the men of the six armies.
On the Gēngchén day,
the Son of Heaven campaigned eastward.
On the Guǐwèi day,
he arrived at Wù [something] Mountain.
This was where the Zhì clan resided.
[Someone] of the Zhì clan went to meet the Son of Heaven at Wù [something] Mountain,
presenting as gifts two white side-horses,
forty wild horses and wild oxen,
and seventy guard dogs.
He then offered four hundred food-horses,
and three thousand cattle and sheep.
He said:
The Zhì clan [invited] the Son of Heaven to travel north to [a certain] marsh.
The men of the Zhì clan presented one hundred [jars] of wine to the Son of Heaven.
The Son of Heaven bestowed upon them patterned dog-fur,
two times nine golden urns,
forty shell-decorated belts,
three hundred bundles of cinnabar pearls,
and one hundred [measures] of cinnamon and ginger. They prostrated in reverence and received them.
On the Yǐyǒu day,
the Son of Heaven campaigned southward,
turning eastward.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
he arrived at the Xiàn River.
He then proceeded eastward on campaign.
He drank and then set out,
heading southeast.
On the Jǐhài day,
he arrived at Guā Lú Mountain,
which was surrounded threefold like a city wall.
This was the stronghold of the Èshì and Húshì clans.
The Son of Heaven then proceeded eastward on campaign,
crossing south over sandy plains.
On the Xīnchǒu day,
the Son of Heaven grew thirsty on the sandy plains,
and before drink could be found,
a warrior of the Seven Elite Troops named Gāo Bēnróng stabbed the neck of the left side-horse,
took its clear blood, and gave it to the Son of Heaven to drink.
The Son of Heaven praised him,
and bestowed upon Bēnróng a piece of jade pendant.
Bēnróng bowed twice and kowtowed.
The Son of Heaven then proceeded southward on campaign.
On the Jiǎchén day,
he arrived at the edge of Jī Mountain,
where there were蔓柏 trees.
A man named Mìng Huái from [a certain] place presented wine to the Son of Heaven.
The Son of Heaven bestowed upon him a golden urn,
a shell-decorated belt,
and seventy bundles of cinnabar.
Mìng Huái prostrated in reverence and received them.
On the Yǐsì day,
[someone] named Zhū Zhān presented wine to the Son of Heaven.
The Son of Heaven bestowed upon him a golden urn,
a shell-decorated belt,
and seventy bundles of cinnabar.
Zhū Zhān prostrated in reverence and received them.
《Ancient Text》.
On the day Gēngchén,
they reached the Tāo River.
This was the territory of the Zhuóyáo clan.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Son of Heaven journeyed eastward.
On the day Guǐwèi,
they reached Sū Valley.
This was the land of the Gǔgān clan.
Then they journeyed southward,
turning east.
On the day Bǐngxū,
they reached Chángshān,
the western border of the Chóngzī clan.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Son of Heaven ascended Chángshān.
Then he journeyed eastward.
On the day Gēngyín,
they reached the banks of the Black River of the Chóngzī clan.
Here there was wild wheat,
here there was moss and violets,
what the Xīmó people call "tree grain,"
which the Chóngzī clan ate.
Here there was the Mountain of Colored Stones,
which the Chóngzī clan guarded.
It was said:
"Zhīsī,
Xuánguī,
Xuányáo,
Lánggān,
Jiānzhēn,
Wánlǐ,
Yúqí,
Mínwěi,
all fine stone vessels came from here."
In the first month of autumn, on the day Guǐsì,
the Son of Heaven ordered the Chóngzī clan to provide food for his retinue for five days.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Son of Heaven ascended the Mountain of Colored Stones,
and there he gathered colored stones.
The Son of Heaven had the people of the Chóngzī clan cast them into vessels on the banks of the Black River,
producing an endless array of utensils, garments, objects, and fine ornaments.
It is said the Son of Heaven rested for a month.
In autumn, on the day Guǐhài,
the Son of Heaven feasted the people of the Chóngzī clan, Guān’é,
and bestowed upon them eighteen golden jars,
one silver bird,
fifty shell-decorated belts,
seven hundred bundles of pearls,
bamboo arrows,
a hundred hampers of cinnamon and ginger,
and silk from the Diāoguān.
Guān’é then performed a膜拜 (mó bài) and received them.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Son of Heaven journeyed eastward,
and Guān’é escorted the Son of Heaven to the mountains of Chángshā.
[Missing text].
The Son of Heaven had Bó Yāo receive it.
Bó Yāo said:
"The ancestors of the Chóngzī clan
were from the Sānmiáo clan's territory."
With yellow wood and silver ornaments, they performed a膜拜 (mó bài) and received it.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Son of Heaven journeyed eastward,
turning south.
On the day Jǐsì,
they reached Wén Mountain,
where the Xīmó people called [missing text] feasted the Son of Heaven at Wén Mountain.
The Xīmó people then offered three hundred food horses,
two thousand cattle and sheep,
a thousand carts of millet,
and the Son of Heaven had Bì Jǔ receive them.
It is said the Son of Heaven toured Wén Mountain for three days,
and there he gathered colored stones.
On the day Rényín,
the Son of Heaven drank at the foot of Wén Mountain.
The people of Wén Mountain, Guīyí, then offered forty fine horses,
three hundred oxen,
ninety guard dogs,
and two hundred fāng oxen.
The Son of Heaven's豪馬 (háo mǎ),豪牛 (háo niú),
dragon dogs,
豪羊 (háo yáng),

On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Son of Heaven journeyed northward.
On the day Wùyín,
he lodged by the river,
and there gathered his paternal and fraternal kin, the royal ministers, and the women of the Jī clan to complete the mourning rites with weeping,
concluding the mourning at Áoshì.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Son of Heaven crossed the river westward,
at the ford of Áoshì.
On the day Gēngchén,
he lodged at Máochǐ,
where he performed the yīn sacrifice to end the mourning period,
began playing music again,
and returned in plain garments,
so it was called Sùshì.
The Son of Heaven then proceeded southwest.
On the day Guǐwèi,
he reached Yěwáng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Son of Heaven ascended northward up the great northern slope,
and descended to rest beneath two cypress trees.
The Son of Heaven, dwelling in perpetual sorrow and heartache,
then thought of the virtuous one, Shèng Jī,
and shed tears.
The warriors of the Seven Elite Troops, Yāo Yù, admonished the Son of Heaven, saying:
"Since ancient times, there has been death and life—
how could it be only the virtuous one?
The Son of Heaven finds no joy,
emerging from perpetual longing.
Perpetual longing brings benefit,
but do not forget what is new."
The Son of Heaven grieved at this,
and again shed tears,
but on that day he ceased.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Son of Heaven crossed westward over the Xíng slope.
He then proceeded southwest.
On the day Wùzǐ,
he reached Yán.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Son of Heaven ascended southward up the slope of Tiánlíng on Mount Bó,
and lodged at Yú.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Son of Heaven journeyed southward.
On the auspicious day Xīnmǎo,
the Son of Heaven entered Nánzhèng.
